articles.title: Felício Ramuth é o 1º vice reeleito em SP em 28 anos; conheça o número 2 do estado | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-prefeito de São José dos Campos, Ramuth foi escolhido por Tarcísio de Freitas em 2022, meses após dizer que o governador era um 'péssimo exemplo' e que chegava a São Paulo para 'tirar votos do cidadão' antes de 'entregar algo ao estado'.
articles.summary: Ex-prefeito de São José dos Campos, Ramuth foi escolhido por Tarcísio de Freitas em 2022, meses após dizer que o governador era um 'péssimo exemplo' e que chegava a São Paulo para 'tirar votos do cidadão' antes de 'entregar algo ao estado'.
articles.body:
Os pré-candidatos ao governo de São Paulo Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) e Felício Ramuth (MDB). — Foto: Acervo pessoal

Felício Ramuth (MDB) foi reeleito vice-governador de São Paulo na chapa de Tarcísio de Freitas ( Republicanos ), vencedor da disputa no estado em 2026, e se tornou o primeiro vice-governador paulista a se reeleger em 28 anos.

O último a conseguir o mesmo feito havia sido Geraldo Alckmin, que foi eleito vice-governador em 1994 e reeleito em 1998, ambas as vezes na chapa de Mário Covas. Alckmin assumiu o governo em 2001, após a morte de Covas.

A permanência dele na chapa não foi fácil e envolveu uma disputa política interna nos meses que antecederam a eleição. Ele precisou "superar" nomes como Gilberto Kassab , Valdemar Costa Neto e até Ricardo Nunes ( leia mais abaixo ).

A trajetória política de Ramuth começou em São José dos Campos , no Vale do Paraíba. Empresário, formado em Administração e com MBA em Gestão Pública pela Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV), ele nasceu na capital paulista, mas ainda jovem foi para o interior e assumiu o negócio da família.

Antes de disputar eleições, passou por cargos na administração municipal. Em 2005, tornou-se presidente da Urbanizadora Municipal de São José dos Campos (Urbam). Depois, foi secretário municipal de Transportes e secretário de Projetos Especiais de Comunicação.

Em 2016, disputou pela primeira vez um cargo eletivo e foi eleito prefeito de São José dos Campos. Na ocasião, recebeu 219.511 votos, a maior votação da história do município. Depois, foi reeleito no 1º turno e deixou a prefeitura em abril de 2022.

A chegada de Ramuth à chapa de Tarcísio começou a ser desenhada ainda no início de 2022. Depois de 28 anos filiado ao PSDB , Ramuth deixou o partido em janeiro daquele ano e se filiou ao PSD , a convite do presidente nacional da legenda, Gilberto Kassab.

Na época, em entrevista ao g1 , Ramuth afirmou que sua saída do PSDB também havia sido motivada por divergências com o então governador João Doria durante a pandemia de Covid-19.

Ele até cogitou concorrer ao cargo de governador como cabeça de chapa, mas o PSD decidiu apoiar Tarcísio, o que rendeu uma vaga de vice na chapa.

Antes de ser aliado, Ramuth criticou Tarcísio de Freitas em função de seu domicílio eleitoral em 2022:

"O fato de ele ser carioca, ser de outro estado, independentemente dessa questão legal e moral... São Paulo foi construído por pessoas que vêm de fora. Nesse aspecto não vejo problema. A diferença é que, quem vem de fora, vem pra oferecer ao estado primeiro e depois colher. Aqui é o contrário: ele vem pra tirar votos do cidadão para depois entregar algo ao estado. Não sei se o cidadão do estado vai ver isso com bons olhos", completou.

O hoje vice se referia a um inquérito do Ministério Público que apurava a mudança de domicílio eleitoral de Tarcísio do estado do Rio de Janeiro para São Paulo . Meses depois, a promotoria solicitou uma investigação da Polícia Federal.

Um dos pedidos para a investigação, arquivada meses depois , foi feito pelo PSOL, que argumentou que a transferência de domicílio eleitoral de Freitas aconteceu "às vésperas do pleito".

A assessoria de Tarcísio disse que o então pré-candidato tinha um contrato de aluguel em São José dos Campos e que a mudança de seu domicílio eleitoral se deu de forma legal.Disputa pela vaga em 2026

Este ano, Ramuth já ocupava o cargo de vice-governador, mas precisava garantir sua permanência na chapa para disputar a reeleição ao lado de Tarcísio. A vaga passou a ser alvo de uma disputa entre diferentes grupos políticos.

O presidente nacional do PL, Valdemar Costa Neto, chegou a defender que o então presidente da Assembleia Legislativa, André do Prado (PL), fosse escolhido para a posição;

No entanto, o próprio Ramuth defendia que Prado poderia ser um bom nome para a segunda vaga ao Senado por São Paulo, o que acabou acontecendo;

Além do PL, Kassab também manifestou interesse pelo posto ao declarar publicamente que se sentiria “privilegiado” caso fosse convidado para a chapa de Tarcísio;

Até o prefeito de São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes (MDB), demonstrou interesse em indicar o vice da chapa.

Mas, nos bastidores, a possibilidade de Tarcísio manter Ramuth ganhou força. Conforme apurado pelo g1 , a lealdade demonstrada pelo vice ao longo do governo foi um dos fatores determinantes para a manutenção dele no cargo.

A definição ocorreu no início de maio: Tarcísio confirmou Felício como candidato a vice e anunciou, no mesmo dia, André do Prado e Guilherme Derrite (PP) como candidatos ao Senado na chapa.

A permanência na chapa também levou Ramuth a mudar novamente de partido em 2026. Em uma publicação nas redes sociais, ele anunciou a saída do PSD e a filiação ao MDB, afirmou que a mudança representava “um novo passo” em sua trajetória política e disse que a decisão estava alinhada ao projeto político de Tarcísio.

Já Kassab afirmou que a saída foi uma decisão do próprio PSD, que pediu para Ramuth deixar o partido.

“Como o Felício estava em voo solo, se posicionando sobre querer ser vice independentemente da questão partidária, eu o convidei a sair. Comuniquei o Tarcísio, e ele saiu. Simples assim”, afirmou Kassab.

Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) junto com o vice do PSD, Felício, e Gilberto Kassab. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Em busca feita do sistema do Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo pela reportagem do g1 é possível encontrar diversas ações de reparação por danos morais que Ramuth moveu contra críticos da gestão dele em São José dos Campos nas redes sociais.

Parte das publicações alvo de processo por parte do ex-prefeito apresentam xingamentos pessoais, chamando o político de vagabundo, safado, "felixo", entre outras ofensas e fake news.

“Os processos que movi são contra pessoas que extrapolaram o limite da crítica política da minha gestão, ofendendo a minha honra pessoal, espalhando notícias faltas ou usando a minha condição de deficiente físico estrábico para me atacar. Isso não admito de forma alguma”, declarou o candidato a vice do PSD.

articles.title: Quem é Tarcísio de Freitas, que assume pela segunda vez o governo de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Carioca, ex-capitão do Exército e engenheiro civil, governador reeleito construiu a carreira no serviço público antes de disputar sua primeira eleição em 2022.
articles.summary: Carioca, ex-capitão do Exército e engenheiro civil, governador reeleito construiu a carreira no serviço público antes de disputar sua primeira eleição em 2022.
articles.body:
O governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas, durante entrevista coletiva — Foto: Rafael Peixoto/g1

Antes estreante no mundo da política, a partir de 6 de janeiro Tarcísio de Freitas ( Republicanos ) assume pela segunda vez o comando de São Paulo, o estado mais populoso do país.

Com 99% das urnas apuradas, ele tinha 62,65% dos votos.

Aos 51 anos, sendo 17 deles dedicados à carreira no Exército 14 ao funcionalismo público federal, Tarcísio foi ministro da Infraestrutura do governo Bolsonaro desde a posse do presidente, em janeiro de 2018, e se apresenta como um “técnico” e “realizador”.

O governador reeleito nasceu no Rio de Janeiro e passou a infância em Brasília. Filho de Maria Alice e Amaury, Tarcísio diz que herdou a fé da mãe e o amor pelo futebol e pelo Flamengo do pai, sua “maior saudade”.

É casado com Cristiane há 28 anos, com quem tem dois filhos, Matheus, de 27 anos, e Letícia, de 19.

Aos 17 anos, Tarcísio foi para Campinas e cursou o último ano do Ensino Médio na escola preparatória de cadetes do Exército. Apesar de votar em São José dos Campos, ele nunca morou na cidade do Vale do Paraíba, onde vivem familiares.

Em 1996, se formou em ciências militares pela Academia Militar de Agulhas Negras (Aman) e passou a atuar como oficial do Exército. Em 2002, concluiu a graduação em engenharia civil e tornou-se engenheiro do Exército.

Além de Rio e São Paulo, viveu também em Pernambuco, no Rio Grande do Norte, no Amazonas e no Haiti, onde serviu o Brasil como chefe da seção de engenharia do Exército em uma missão de paz das Organizações das Nações Unidas (ONU). Foi um período que deixou marcas: desenvolveu síndrome do pânico, sintoma de uma depressão que precisou tratar com remédios por dois anos.

Deixou a carreira militar em 2008, com a patente de capitão, e entrou para o funcionalismo público federal. Foi diretor-executivo e diretor-geral do DNIT (Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes), além de ter atuado como secretário da Coordenação da Secretaria Especial do Programa de Parceria de Investimentos, durante os governos de Dilma Rousseff e Michel Temer.

Em dezembro de 2018, foi nomeado ministro da Infraestrutura pelo presidente Jair Bolsonaro ( PL ), onde ficou até 2022. Por causa das obras de pavimentação pelo país, recebeu o apelido de “Tarcisão do Asfalto''. Também teve destaque nas privatizações: sua gestão fez 81 pregões (de aeroportos, terminais portuários, ferrovias e rodovias).

Em março de 2022, se filiou ao Republicanos, partido do Centrão que integra a base do governo do presidente no Congresso e encarou sua primeira campanha eleitoral, que culminou com a vitória.

Se em 2022, para ganhar votos, se aproximou do discurso do padrinho político, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL), quatro anos depois, optou por uma estratégia diferente com Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), que disputa a Presidência: apesar de ir às ruas com Flávio em atos, deixou para gravar participação na propaganda eleitoral do candidato do PL na reta final da campanha.

Declarou à Justiça Eleitoral possuir bens no valor de R$ 2,6 milhões. Na eleição de 2022, havia declarado R$ 2,3 milhões. Sua coligação é a Coragem para Seguir Avançando, formada pelos partidos Republicanos, PL, MDB, Democrata, Avante, PSD, Federação Renovação Solidária (PRD e Solidariedade) e Federação União Progressista (União e PP).

O candidato à reeleição ao governo do Estado de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) fez caminhada na região central de São Paulo, nesta sexta-feira (2), acompanhado do prefeito da cidade, Ricardo Nunes e do candidato ao Senado, André do Prado (PL). — Foto: ALOISIO MAURICIO/FOTOARENA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

articles.title: Veja a repercussão internacional do resultado das eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículos internacionais destacaram que nenhum candidato conseguiu votos suficientes para se eleger no primeiro turno e noticiaram Flávio à frente de Lula.
articles.summary: Veículos internacionais destacaram que nenhum candidato conseguiu votos suficientes para se eleger no primeiro turno e noticiaram Flávio à frente de Lula.
articles.body:
O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vão disputar o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais no próximo dia 25. Com 99,94% das urnas apuradas, Flávio tinha 47,04% dos votos, contra 45,15% de Lula.

Após a confirmação do resultado do 1º turno, veículos de imprensa internacionais repercutiram a disputa entre os dois candidatos. Veja abaixo como a eleição foi noticiada:

O jornal norte-americano The New York Times destacou que nenhum dos dois candidatos conseguiu o número de votos suficiene para vencer no 1º turno.

"Lula e filho de Bolsonaro vão ao segundo turno na disputa pela Presidência do Brasil", diz o título da reportagem.

The Guardian Flávio x Lula — Foto: Reprodução

O britânico The Guardian destacou que Flávio terminou a apuração do primeiro turno na frente de Lula.

"A corrida presidencial brasileira vai para o segundo turno, com Flávio Bolsonaro à frente do atual presidente Lula", diz o título.

Reuters Flávio x Lula — Foto: Reprodução

A agência de notícias Reuters classificou o desempenho de Flávio como além das expectativas.

"Bolsonaro supera expectativas na eleição presidencial brasileira e enfrenta Lula no segundo turno", diz o título.

A agência da notícias norte-americana também destacou que nenhum dos dois candidatos conseguiu o número suficiente de votos.

"O Brasil vai para o segundo turno das eleições após Bolsonaro e Lula não conseguirem a maioria dos votos", afirma o título.

Já a britânica BBC destacou a posição de Flávio Bolsonaro à frente de Lula.

"As eleições no Brasil vão para o segundo turno, com a vitória do direitista Flávio Bolsonaro no primeiro turno", afirma o título.

Le Monde Flávio x Lula — Foto: Reprodução

O jornal francês Le Monde destacou a relação de Flávio com jair Bolsonaro e informou que ele saiu na frente no 1º turno.

"Eleições presidenciais no Brasil: Flávio Bolsonaro, filho do ex-presidente de extrema-direita, está à frente de Lula e o enfrentará no segundo turno", diz o título.

O Argentin Clarín classificou o resultado como uma "surpresa".

Al Jazeera Flávio x Lula — Foto: Reprodução

"As urnas fecharam no Brasil em uma eleição polarizada que colocou Lula contra Bolsonaro", afirma o título.

A confirmação de que haverá segundo turno foi anunciada pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) neste domingo (4), às 20h56, quando 96,78% das urnas já tinham sido apuradas. Àquela altura, Flávio Bolsonaro tinha 47,39% dos votos, e Lula, tinha 44,74%.

Às 22h10, conforme o TSE, Flávio estava com 47,07%, mais de 56 milhões de votos. Já Lula estava com 45,12%, mais de 53,7 milhões de votos.

Daqui a três semanas, os eleitores voltam às urnas para definir se Flávio Bolsonaro governará o país pelos próximos quatro anos ou se Lula terá um quarto mandato presidencial .

Se Flávio for eleito, tomará posse, aos 45 anos, no dia 5 de janeiro de 2027, na cadeira ocupada por seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro, entre 2019 e 2022.

Se vencer, Lula assumirá o quarto mandato aos 81 anos e será o primeiro brasileiro a presidir o país quatro vezes.

Flávio e Lula deixaram para trás Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo), Edmilson Dias (PCB), Hertz Dias (PSTU), Samara Martins (UP), Wilson Grassi (Democrata), Clariana Barão (DC) e Rui Costa Pimenta (PCO).

articles.title: In 1981, Carole King bought a 128-acre Idaho ranch and spent 20 years restoring it; after adding a recording studio and two pools, the 35-year residence was later sold for $3.999 million
articles.summary: On the cover of Tapestry, Carole King sits in a window seat with a cat, with sunlight filtering through Indian-cloth curtains.
articles.body: On the cover of Tapestry, Carole King sits in a window seat with a cat, with sunlight filtering through Indian-cloth curtains. The album cover, released in 1971, represented a simple, cosy home life, much like King’s music. But her own version of home turned out to be a good deal bigger, and a long way from any neighbour.Carole King bought the ranch in Stanley, Idaho, in 1981 and worked on it for decades. After spending 35 years at the residence, the Robinson Bar Ranch was sold for $3.99 million.Somewhere wilderCarole King was born in Brooklyn and raised there. She wrote her early songs in Manhattan before moving to California. While living in Los Angeles, she began looking for somewhere ‘a little wilder’. She explored several Western states before finding something that connected with her in central Idaho. That place was Robinson Bar Ranch, a 128-acre property surrounded by forest near Stanley, Idaho.For her, even the flat ground below the mountains felt restorative, so she purchased the property. The ranch sits where Warm Springs Creek meets the Salmon River, inside the Sawtooth National Recreation Area. Reaching it means leaving Highway 75 for a Forest Service road that tracks the river until the canyon opens into irrigated meadows. Ketchum and Sun Valley lie under 90 minutes south.A place with historyIn the late 1800s, the Robinson Bar was a mining claim. Around 1916, Chase Addison Clark homesteaded it and expanded the lodge. He later became governor of Idaho. The Clark family owned the land for more than 70 years, according to Hall & Hall, the brokerage that handled the sale. Clark’s daughter Bethine married Senator Frank Church, whose legislation helped protect the Central Idaho wilderness and the recreation area that now surrounds the ranch. Over the years, the ranch also welcomed guests, became a cross-country ski resort and a French country-style inn.Carole King bought it in 1981.Restoring the ranchFor King, restoring the property meant changing what needed changing and keeping what made the place itself. So she kept the original footprint of the ranch intact and gave its walls and ceilings some structural upgrades.The work stretched across nearly two decades and two major remodels. Robert C. Wyllie handled most of the construction and much of the design. Dave Selene contributed metalwork. King’s daughter, Sherry Goffin Kondor, helped shape the interiors alongside the design firm Citizen Properties. King, on the other hand, carried the role of a coordinator rather than an artist. She said yes to good ideas.So old roofs were replaced with Cor-Ten steel, with dormers added to pull in light. When a giant spruce came down in the nearby forest, she got permission to mill it on site. It became panelling in the log-built recording studio.The hot springs became a blessing. Gravity-fed spring water warmed the floors in the lodge’s kitchen and baths. Geothermal heat also runs through the lodge and studio and fills two pools. As the studio’s Steinway needed steady warmth, this arrangement only helped. The rest of the compound looks like a small village. There is a stone poolhouse carved into a hillside. Eight guest cabins have electricity but no running water. There are two barns, a wood shop, a greenhouse and a chicken house. The five-bedroom lodge holds roughly 7,300 square feet. King has said that no place she has lived felt more like home than this one.The ranch was first listed in 2006 for $19 million. After problems with a bridge on the Forest Service road, the listing was taken off. It returned in 2010 at $16 million. By late 2015, Hall & Hall was asking $9.9 million. According to the broker, such properties don’t often appear on the market. “It isn’t often that a property this unique comes up for sale,” the broker said. “When you close the ranch gate behind you, the clock is turned back to another time and the incredible soul of this place will change one’s life.”The brokerage’s listing page now marks the ranch as sold, with a last asking price of $3,999,000.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Abducted Kuki farmer found dead with hands tied in Manipur's Kangpokpi
articles.summary: Kuki farmer Hemjang Haokip, 71, found dead with hands tied in Manipur’s Kangpokpi after alleged abduction; village body alleges torture and militant role.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: The body of a 71-year-old Kuki farmer, Hemjang Haokip, was recovered on Sunday from a remote forest area in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district with his hands tied, hours after suspected Naga militants allegedly abducted him from his field hut before setting it on fire on Saturday.According to the local village council, Haokip was likely tortured and beaten to death as his body bore injury marks, suggesting that he had been brutally assaulted, sources said.While security forces managed to recover his body, with the aid of sniffer dogs, after Haokip’s clothes were found near his field hut, it was the villagers who brought it out of the forest area in the presence of security personnel.The Kuki Youth Organisation’s Leimakhong block condemned the killing, describing it as a “pre-planned murder”.Alleging involvement of NSCN-IM and Tangkhul elements in Haokip’s killing, the youth organization, in a statement, said, “The circumstances and condition in which he was found is horrifying and have sent shockwaves throughout the Kuki community. The involvement of NSCN-IM and Tangkhul elements in this incident has further intensified the anger and anguish of the community.”The youth body warned that the Kuki community would not remain silent. “We will mobilise every available community mechanism, pursue every avenue, strengthen our collective vigilance, and take every necessary step within our capacity,” it said.On Saturday, the Khunkho Kuki village authority had issued a 24-hour ultimatum to the state authorities and law-enforcement agencies, demanding Haokip’s safe return by Sunday and warning of widespread democratic protests, if he was not found.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Protesters climb barricades, confront police in march against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi; 120 detained
articles.summary: Delhi protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar entered day 3 as protesters clashed with police, faced ~120 detentions; AISA chief Neha Bora alleges abduction.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Minutes before the march was set to begin, police loudspeakers at India Gate were already telling people to leave. Buses stood ready to carry away detainees, and a heavy deployment guarded the proposed starting point.Within the next few hours, the gathering shifted to Ashoka Road, where hundreds of protesters pushed barricades into the path of a riot-control vehicle, climbed barriers and vehicles, and confronted police trying to block them from Jantar Mantar. Sunday, the third consecutive day of protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, saw nearly 120 detentions.At 2.50 pm, police were in force at India Gate. They asked media personnel to keep their identity cards visible. The announcements came a day after three women covering the protests alleged sexual harassment by police personnel.A little after 3 pm, members of AAP and its student wing, ASAP, arrived with other protesters. As they attempted to march, police detained them and took them towards some waiting buses. Some resisted boarding. Others climbed onto a bus and continued chanting. Some protesters broke the rear window of a bus to escape, while some jumped from the moving buses. During the mobilisation, a bus was blocked and detainees freed.For students waiting at India Gate for the march called by All India Students’ Association (AISA) and other Left groups, uncertainty suddenly gave way to a rush towards Ashoka Road.Word spread that the gathering point had shifted to the Andhra Bhawan Circle, and protesters were seen rushing there. Soon, hundreds had assembled. The march stalled at India Gate had found a new gathering point and a fresh line of police to confront.As police arrived in large numbers and a riot-control vehicle approached, the protesters pushed barricades into its path, blocking its movement. Some clambered onto the barriers and continued shouting slogans as police tried to contain the crowd. The barricades became the centre of a face-off.Around 5 pm, the confrontation shifted to a vehicle near Shangri-La hotel, where AISA president Neha Bora was taken, according to a complaint the organisation sent the Delhi Police commissioner. Women protesters tried to climb onto the vehicle, while women police personnel struggled to pull them away. Bora reportedly also scaled a barricade. Protesters later marched towards the Windsor Place roundabout too. Traffic was severely affected around the area.Apart from the common cause of demanding Kumar’s resignation, for some in the crowd, anger over police’s way of handling of the protests was another reason to turn up. “Even if prohibitory orders have been imposed, we want to march,” said Mannat, an artist. “When police themselves are attacking women, don’t the rules apply to them?”Women from various colleges said they had joined the marches demanding safer public spaces. Their concerns about women’s safety now extended to the treatment of protesters and journalists. Suhana, a participant, said she had returned because of what she described as police brutality Saturday. She alleged that she had been detained at 1.30 pm. “I was touched inappropriately by police personnel. Police acknowledged my written complaint with a stamp, but neither registered an FIR, nor arranged for a medical examination,” she said.In its complaint, AISA alleged that male police personnel without badges had taken Bora away in a vehicle. No woman police officer was there. The organisation described this as an “abduction”. An AISA member later said Bora was released in the Narela industrial area police station but did not have her phone or bag.Police had said permission had not been granted for the marches.Later in the day, Indian Youth Congress workers marched from Raisina Road towards Jantar Mantar. articles.standfirst: Candidato recebeu 27.328 votos, o equivalente a 0,70% dos votos válidos no estado.
articles.summary: Leandro Bello (PSB) recebeu 27.328 votos e foi eleito deputado estadual pelo Maranhão nas Eleições 2026.
articles.body:
Leandro Bello (PSB) foi eleito deputado estadual pelo Maranhão nas Eleições 2026, com 27.328 votos, o equivalente a 0,70% dos votos válidos no estado.

Ele foi o 42º candidato mais votado do estado para o cargo. O município em que teve mais votos foi Maranhão (27.328 votos).

Leandro Bello foi reeleito e cumprirá seu 2º mandato consecutivo na Assembleia Legislativa do Maranhão.

Veja o perfil do eleito na página Quem são os candidatos , publicada pelo g1 e atualizada com dados fornecidos pelo TSE.

Os deputados estaduais eleitos em 2026 tomam posse em 1º de fevereiro de 2027, para mandatos de quatro anos.

Na Assembleia Legislativa, as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional: o número de cadeiras depende do total de votos que cada legenda recebeu, e não apenas da votação individual de cada candidato.

articles.standfirst: Partidos que apoiaram reeleição do governador Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) elegeram 65 dos 94 deputados da Alesp, garantindo ampla maioria na próxima legislatura.
articles.summary: Partidos que apoiaram reeleição do governador Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) elegeram 65 dos 94 deputados da Alesp, garantindo ampla maioria na próxima legislatura.
articles.body:
Fachada da Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo (Alesp) — Foto: José Antonio Teixeira/Alesp/Divulgação

O PL confirmou neste domingo (4) sua posição como principal força política da Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo (Alesp) e ampliou significativamente sua presença na Casa pelo segundo ciclo eleitoral consecutivo. Depois de eleger 19 deputados em 2022, o partido chegou a 21 integrantes ao longo da legislatura e agora conquistou 27 cadeiras para o mandato que começa em 2027.

O PT manteve a segunda maior bancada, mas encolheu dos atuais 17 parlamentares para 16 eleitos para a próxima legislatura. Também na oposição, o PSOL praticamente dobrou sua representação atual, saltando de cinco para nove deputados estaduais.

O resultado fortalece a base do governador reeleito Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos). Somados, os partidos que apoiaram sua candidatura à reeleição — PL, PSD, União Brasil, Podemos, PP, Republicanos, MDB, Novo, PRD e PSDB — elegeram 65 dos 94 deputados estaduais da próxima legislatura. O resultado garante ao Palácio dos Bandeirantes uma maioria confortável na Assembleia Legislativa, equivalente a mais de dois terços das cadeiras da Casa.

A bancada do PL foi impulsionada pela votação recorde de Eduarda Campopiano, que recebeu 1.956.238 votos e se tornou a segunda deputada estadual mais votada da história do estado . Sozinha, ela obteve cerca de 8,4% dos votos válidos para deputado estadual, votação foi suficiente para assegurar aproximadamente outras sete vagas ao partido na Assembleia Legislativa.

Fenômeno semelhante ocorreu com Eduardo Suplicy, segundo candidato mais votado do estado. Com 654.627 votos, ele ajudou a garantir cerca duas cadeiras adicionais ao PT.

articles.title: Segundo turno no DF: veja pesquisas de Celina Leão x Leandro Grass | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisas realizadas antes do primeiro turno apontaram vantagem de Celina Leão em confrontos diretos com Leandro Grass; candidatos voltam às urnas em 25 de outubro.
articles.summary: Pesquisas realizadas antes do primeiro turno apontaram vantagem de Celina Leão em confrontos diretos com Leandro Grass; candidatos voltam às urnas em 25 de outubro.
articles.body:
Celina Leão (PP) e Leandro Grass (PT), candidatos ao governo do Distrito Federal, em imagens de arquivo — Foto: Reprodução

Celina Leão (PP) e Leandro Grass (PT) vão disputar o 2º turno para governador no Distrito Federal. O resultado foi anunciado na noite deste domingo (4) pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

Com 100% das seções apuradas neste domingo (4), Celina Leão terminou o primeiro turno com 49,93% dos votos válidos (825.530 votos). Leandro Grass obteve 34,47% (569.930 votos).

Desde o início da campanha, as pesquisas de intenção de voto já indicavam esse cenário como uma possibilidade – que ganhou ainda mais força desde a saída de Arruda (PSD) da disputa , 10 dias antes do primeiro turno.

Antevendo essa possibilidade, a Quaest e o Datafolha testaram, nas pesquisas, como seria uma disputa direta entre Celina e Grass. Todos os resultados desse segundo turno hipotético, simulados ainda no primeiro turno, apontam vantagem de Celina.

Como Celina não ultrapassou 50% dos votos válidos ( por pouco mais de mil votos ), eleitores do DF voltam às urnas no próximo dia 25 para escolher governador(a) e presidente da República .

Na véspera do primeiro turno, os dois institutos projetaram uma possível vitória de Celina Leão no primeiro turno. Ainda assim, testaram também um possível segundo turno entre Celina e Grass.

A Quaest divulgada em 3 de outubro apontou, em um eventual segundo turno, 62% dos votos válidos para Celina Leão e 38% para Leandro Grass.

O levantamento ouviu 2.652 eleitores. A margem de erro é de 2% pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número DF-04089/2026 .

Veja abaixo os números de todas as rodadas desse cenário no primeiro turno:

Quaest, 3 de outubro: intenção de votos para governador do DF, 2º turno — Foto: Arte/g1

Já o Datafolha divulgado também na véspera do primeiro turno apontou 56% das intenções de voto para Celina Leão e 31% para Leandro Grass no cenário de segundo turno.

Indecisos eram 3% e branco, nulo ou não vai votar somavam 9%.

O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e pela Folha de S. Paulo e ouviu 1.620 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais, entre os dias 2 e 3 de outubro. A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número DF-07243/2026.

Datafolha, 3 de outubro: intenção de votos para governador do DF, 2º turno — Foto: Arte/g1

Assim, todos os cenários de confronto direto entre Celina e Grass antes do primeiro turno colocavam Celina à frente.

Pesquisas eleitorais, no entanto, registram a intenção de voto no momento em que as entrevistas são realizadas e não representam o resultado da eleição.

Veja abaixo o perfil dos dois candidatos, em ordem alfabética.

Michelle Bolsonaro (PL), Celina Leão (PP) e Bia Kicis (PL) — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Celina Leão Hizim Ferreira tem 45 anos, é natural de Goiânia, em Goiás, é administradora e filiado ao Partido Progressista (PP). Ela chegou ao Palácio do Buriti em 2023, como vice na chapa do ex-governador do DF Ibaneis Rocha (MDB).

Celina Leão assumiu como governadora do DF no dia 30 de março, após Ibaneis deixar o cargo para se candidatar ao Senado nas eleições de 2026, embora ele tenha anunciado desistência 4 meses depois.

Antes de assumir o cargo de vice-governadora, Celina Leão atuou como deputada federal pelo DF, também pelo PP, entre 2019 e 2022. A ex-parlamentar se licenciou do mandato por sete meses em 2020, quando assumiu a Secretaria de Esporte e Lazer do Distrito Federal, no primeiro mandato de Ibaneis.

Ela deixou a pasta para participar das eleições para a presidência da Câmara dos Deputados e foi uma das principais articuladoras da campanha de Arthur Lira (PP-AL), que venceu a disputa.

Celina Leão também atuou como deputada distrital por dois mandatos consecutivos, entre 2011 e 2019, à época pelo PDT. Ao ser reeleita, em 2015, a ex-parlamentar assumiu a presidência da Casa.

Leandro Antônio Grass Peixoto tem 41 anos, é natural de Brasília , sociólogo e professor, filiado ao Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT).

Essa é a segunda candidatura de Grass para o governo. Em 2022, ele era representante do PV ficou em segundo lugar no pleito com 434 mil votos, equivalente a 26,25% do total – foi derrotado em primeiro turno por Ibaneis Rocha, que conquistou a reeleição.

Entre 2018 e 2022, Grass foi deputado distrital. Entre 2023 e 2026, presidiu o Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (Iphan), vinculado ao Ministério da Cultura. O político deixou o Iphan para se desincompatibilizar e poder disputar as eleições deste ano.

Em 2018 e 2022, Grass disputou as eleições pelo PV. Ele se filiou ao PT em 2005 – atualmente, os dois partidos e o PCdoB formam uma federação e atuam de maneira conjunta em todo o país.

Durante sua campanha, Celina Leão reforçou que assumiu o cargo de governadora em um momento “delicado” – e que, em quatro meses, “buscou soluções ao invés de culpados”. Também buscou se colocar como "qualificada" para comandar o Palácio do Buriti por mais quatro anos.

Líder das pesquisas de intenção de voto desde o início da campanha, foi alvo de críticas pelos seus adversários nos debates e optou por não participar de alguns deles.

Leandro Grass prometeu priorizar a população do DF, melhorando os serviços como transporte, saúde e educação. "Eu conheço de perto a Brasília que não funciona, para todo mundo que vive aqui. Passou da hora de tratar quem mora nas cidades como prioridade", disse na propaganda eleitoral.

Na campanha, Grass apareceu ao lado do presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: Evaristo Sá/AFP e Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) teve seu melhor desempenho proporcional entre os municípios de São Paulo em Saltinho, no interior do estado, onde recebeu 78,71% dos votos, o equivalente a 4.465 votos. Já Lula (PT) alcançou seu maior percentual em Itapura, no norte paulista, na divisa com Mato Grosso do Sul: 62,57%, com 1.583 votos.

Os dados são da apuração de 100% das urnas no estado, concluída às 21h50 deste domingo (4). O levantamento aponta que Flávio venceu em 605 das cidades paulistas, enquanto Lula ficou na frente em 39.

Na capital paulista, Lula foi o candidato mais votado. Ele venceu em 35 das zonas eleitorais da cidade, contra 22 de Flávio Bolsonaro. O petista teve 60,58% dos votos na zona eleitoral 0001, seu melhor desempenho entre as zonas eleitorais da capital. Flávio, por sua vez, chegou a 53,51% na zona 0253.

O candidato do PL venceu na maior parte dos municípios paulistas. Além de Saltinho, sua votação esteve à frente em cidades de diferentes regiões do estado, entre elas Campinas, Ribeirão Preto, São José dos Campos, Sorocaba, Santos, Guarulhos e Jundiaí.

Em Saltinho, Flávio teve 78,71% dos votos, seu maior percentual entre os municípios do estado. Foram 4.465 votos para o candidato.

Lula ficou na frente em 39 municípios, segundo o levantamento. Entre eles estão São Paulo, Diadema, Mauá, São Bernardo do Campo, Carapicuíba, Embu das Artes, Francisco Morato, Franco da Rocha, Itapevi, Itaquaquecetuba, Taboão da Serra e Cubatão.

O melhor resultado proporcional do petista foi em Itapura, onde recebeu 62,57% dos votos, ou 1.583 votos.

No primeiro turno de 2022, o cenário municipal também foi favorável a Jair Bolsonaro (PL), então candidato à reeleição: ele venceu em 515 das 645 cidades paulistas, enquanto Lula ficou na frente em 130 municípios.

Na capital, Lula também venceu naquele ano, com 47,50% dos votos, contra 37,99% de Jair Bolsonaro.

articles.title: PewDiePie’s OpenAI controversy takes a new turn with his “less restricted” Ajax AI
articles.summary: PewDiePie is stepping into the AI race with a project that is less about building the biggest model and more about making AI personal.
articles.body: PewDiePie is stepping into the AI race with a project that is less about building the biggest model and more about making AI personal. Felix Kjellberg has introduced Ajax, a compact language model designed to run locally through his self-hosted Odysseus workspace. The project has also drawn attention because Kjellberg says OpenAI suspended his account twice during development, with one displayed email citing “distillation.” Ajax is built on Alibaba’s Qwen3.5-9B and aims to handle everyday tasks while keeping processing closer to the user’s own hardware.PewDiePie’s Ajax AI model focuses on local, private computingAjax takes a different path from the giant cloud-based models dominating the AI industry. Its foundation, Qwen3.5-9B, has around nine billion parameters, making it far smaller than many frontier systems.That size is part of the appeal. Kjellberg is designing Ajax for practical jobs such as web searches, browsing, emails and calendars rather than trying to compete on every possible AI benchmark.The model is intended to operate as an “always-on” assistant inside Odysseus. A local setup could give users more control over their data and reduce the need to send routine requests to an external server.However, Ajax is still far from a finished consumer product. The project had not published final hardware requirements, independent benchmark results or downloadable model weights when the announcement was made. Its website was still listing the model as “Coming soon.”PewDiePie’s OpenAI controversy adds another layer to AjaxThe most unusual part of the project involves how Kjellberg says he developed Ajax. He wanted to use outputs from a larger AI system to help create training material for his smaller model, a process known as knowledge distillation.OpenAI allows distillation in some contexts, but its terms restrict using its output to develop competing models and prohibit certain forms of automated extraction. Kjellberg says his account was suspended twice while working on Ajax. One email he displayed reportedly cited “distillation” as the reason.OpenAI has not publicly provided a specific explanation for those account actions, so Kjellberg’s account remains the main source for those details.Ajax is also designed to behave differently from many mainstream assistants. Its creators describe its refusal behaviour as having been “ablated” to create a freer system. Kjellberg reportedly used the open-source Heretic tool for this process.Still, the project retains limits around harmful requests. Its safety claims have not undergone an independent assessment, so they should not be treated as proof that Ajax is safe.Kjellberg plans more reinforcement learning, quantisation and benchmarking before a later release. For now, Ajax represents something broader than a celebrity-built chatbot. It reflects a growing interest in smaller AI models that can run locally, offer greater control and reduce dependence on powerful cloud platforms.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Delhi Lakshmi Yojana: Cash in hand, but can Rs 2,500 change women's agency?
articles.summary: By: Kavya Dubey NEW DELHI: 52-year-old Uma, who lives in Harijan camp at Lodhi Road, is happy to know she will have something added to her savings every
articles.body: By: Kavya DubeyNEW DELHI: 52-year-old Uma, who lives in Harijan camp at Lodhi Road, is happy to know she will have something added to her savings every month, thanks to the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana.Her daughter has just started college, and Uma had been concerned about having enough funds for her wedding.For Priti (29), the monthly stipend of Rs 2,500 means only one thing - nurturing her 10-year-old daughter's inclination towards studies. For the resident of Burari's Nathupura in north Delhi, the vision of her family's future is pegged on her child's education."She wants to be a teacher," she proudly told TOI. And what does Priti want? "Bachchon ke baad, apni ichhayen khatam ho gayi (after my children were born, my desires ended)," she said, attending to her squealing three-year-old son.Sumitra (35), who lives near Kotla Mubarakpur, too, had long lived with a similar thought. Her life revolves around raising her sons, aged 15 and 13, and supporting her husband.But with the stipend she awaits, a wish buried beneath the weight of responsibilities quietly made its way to her heart once again.Sumitra wanted to learn tailoring. But a six-month course costs Rs 4,000-5,000.With her husband's salary of Rs 20,000 a month, Sumitra's home runs on a tight budget: Rs 5,000 for rent, about Rs 10,000 for food and groceries, and the remaining for her sons' education and household expenses.But now, she is thinking beyond her home-bound roles - she wants to learn tailoring, start something of her own and contribute more to the household. "I would be very happy if she earns her own money," said her husband, who works as a peon.During the 2025 assembly polls, BJP-led Delhi govt had announced it would grant Rs 2,500 monthly assistance to women from economically weaker families.The move aims to give such women greater financial security and the ability to make decisions independently, CM Rekha Gupta had said.Some relief, but with income ridersAccording to economist Rajiv Kumar, chairperson, Pahle India Foundation and former vice-chairperson of Niti Aayog, while the scheme offers crucial savings for women, the income eligibility can exclude many."Any additional income does provide some relief. But the criterion of family income being less than Rs 2.5 lakh annually is a bit tough - it implies a monthly income of less than Rs 21,000 per family or less than Rs 700 per day," Kumar said, adding it implies per capita income of less than Rs 200 per day for a family of four.Kumar pointed out that as per official data tabled in March, Delhi's per capita income was projected to be Rs 5.3 lakh for 2025-26. "We could have chosen a higher cut-off," he noted.Anjali (38), a resident of Shidipura, Karol Bagh, earns Rs 7,000 a month packing pens and other articles in a godown close to her home. Her husband has neither a fixed job nor a fixed salary.However, despite her unstable resources, she is adept at managing her household, and the couple together plans a month ahead."There are plenty of problems, but we face them and move on," she said. The uncompromised expenditure in her household is her 15-year-old son's school and tuition fee - Rs 2,000- 3,000 a month.Her "cooperative" septuagenarian in-laws, in whose house the entire family lives, offer her support and relief.The inflation factorFor households in this income group which may not anticipate a rise in prices of essentials, how much does a welfare scheme like Lakshmi Yojana help?"Since Delhi has such a high average per capita income, the existence of a substantial population of families living on less than Rs 2.5 lakh a year is indicative of high inequality. This is a distributional issue," said Shirin Akhter, associate professor of economics at DU's Zakir Husain Delhi College."Consider the recent increase in sugar prices. Govt data show that the all-India average retail price of sugar increased from around Rs 48 per kg in July to over Rs 65 by Aug 26. For a household living close to its subsistence constraint, such increases can require actual changes in consumption. The Rs 2,500 transfer consequently becomes significant," she added.However, for the poorest households, "the expenditure is disproportionately concentrated in necessities", Akhter said."An important question here is: what does the family stop buying? If it is fruit, milk, pulses, today's inflation becomes tomorrow's nutritional deficit. If it is medicines, it becomes a health deficit. If it is tuition, books or schooling, it becomes a human-capital deficit. If the household borrows simply to maintain essential consumption, today's inflation becomes tomorrow's debt burden. And if women compensate by increasing paid work while continuing to carry unpaid household and care responsibilities, inflation also increases women's time poverty," Akhter observed.Navigating aheadThe amount of Rs 2,500 will be credited to the bank accounts of eligible women aged 21 to 60. The beneficiary must be the eldest eligible woman in a family with minimum 10 years' residency in Delhi and should have a valid voter ID.Disqualifying criteria include women who pay income tax, are govt employees or pensioners, are recipients of any pension, owner of a four-wheeler, have more than three children, consume over 2,400 units of electricity annually, or have a govt employee in the family, apart from any criminal antecedent.But is Rs 2,500 enough to alter women's agency? "No," said Kumar. "A regular, reasonably paying employment, once they acquire the required skills, is the only way to alter women's agency," he emphasised."Cash transfers are only a cushion; they aren't a substitute for generating secure jobs or providing good public services. Income support works best when accompanied by affordable food, healthcare, education, transport and other public services," Akhter said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: ‘Gyanesh must quit right away': Opposition backs Justice Bhuyan’s 'SIR strikes at Constitution's heart' remark
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh and Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra backed Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan after his remarks on voting rights
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh and Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra backed Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan after his remarks on voting rights and the disenfranchisement of citizens at an event in Hyderabad.Sharing a video of Bhuyan’s speech in an X post, Ramesh targeted chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and said that Bhuyan had “exposed the CEC lock, stock and barrel”.He also called on Kumar to quit, alleging that his ability to execute what he described as “G2’s illegal orders” had made him “a liability for the country”.TMC MP Mahua Moitra also praised the judge, saying it was rare for a sitting judge to “speak truth to power”. “Kudos to Justice Bhuyan,” she said.'No amount of whataboutery can justify'Speaking at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Bhuyan said the right to vote is integral to the basic structure of the Constitution. He said any process that results in the disenfranchisement of millions of Indian citizens, making them “second-class citizens in their own country” without voting rights, would be intrinsically arbitrary.“No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution,” he said.Bhuyan further said the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, those with voting rights and those without them — and that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 14 and 326. He also said the right to vote or be included in the voters' list cannot be detached from a citizen’s status, comparing it to “taking out the soul from the body”.His remarks came amid the ongoing political and legal controversy over the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: SARAN: The station house officer (SHO) of Maker police station in Bihar’s Saran district was suspended for allegedly brandishing a pistol at flood-affected people during the distribution of relief material.The suspension came after a video purportedly showing the incident went viral on social media.The incident, prima facie, reflects "gross negligence of duty, indiscipline and arbitrariness", said an official statement issued on Sunday."Maker SHO, Sangram Kumar Singh, has been suspended with immediate effect after a video purportedly showing him brandishing his pistol towards the public while distributing flood relief materials in the area went viral on social media," said the statement issued by the Saran SSP's office.Singh will be paid a subsistence allowance as per rules during the suspension period, it added.According to news agency PTI, nearly 9.87 lakh people across 169 gram panchayats in 30 blocks of six Bihar districts have been affected by floods following heavy rainfall in Nepal and adjoining areas in the last week of September.The affected districts include Saran, West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Darbhanga and Muzaffarpur.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: Meta lets go co-founders and employees of AI startup Virtue AI, four months after the company hired them; Andy Stone admits differences over style of working
articles.summary: Meta is letting go of employees from an AI security startup it acquired just months ago.
articles.body: Meta is letting go of employees from an AI security startup it acquired just months ago. The tech giant has reportedly parted ways with Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song, and Sanmi Koyejo, along with other employees, just four months after bringing them into Meta Superintelligence Labs in June. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone confirmed the departures to Semafor and said the arrangement did not work out as planned because of differences in working styles.The move comes after Meta had recruited the Virtue AI team to strengthen its efforts around AI safety, security and frontier risks. The startup had previously worked with companies including Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as the Commerce Department’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).Meta says Virtue AI arrangement did not work outMeta spokesperson Andy Stone confirmed the departures to Semafor and attributed the decision to differences in how the team worked.“Unfortunately, the arrangement didn’t work out as planned,” Stone said, adding that Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.The departures come as Meta continues to shape its AI strategy and expand its capabilities around increasingly advanced AI systems. The company has been investing heavily in artificial intelligence, while AI safety and security have also become a growing focus for technology companies and policymakers.Meta hired Virtue AI founders in JuneIn June, Axios reported that Meta Superintelligence Labs hired Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song and Sanmi Koyejo, along with other members of the startup’s team.The hiring aimed to strengthen Meta’s security efforts around AI agents at a time when concerns about the safety of increasingly capable AI systems were growing.Virtue AI had developed enterprise AI security tools covering automated red teaming, runtime guardrails and AI governance. The startup had also previously worked with Anthropic, OpenAI and the Commerce Department’s NIST. However, the terms of the arrangement were not disclosed.“As we ship AI products to billions of people and build increasingly capable agents, keeping those systems safe, reliable, and trustworthy is foundational,” the memo says.Li and Song were set to report to Nat Friedman, a Meta Superintelligence Labs executive, while Koyejo was expected to report to Rob Fergus, head of Meta's fundamental AI research lab, FAIR.Why Meta hired the Virtue AI teamMeta's decision to bring in the Virtue AI founders reflected the company's broader push to strengthen AI security as it develops more capable models and agents.The startup's work focused on identifying potential risks in AI systems and developing tools to test and safeguard them. Its technology included automated red teaming to identify weaknesses in AI systems, as well as runtime guardrails and governance tools.The hiring also represented another example of Meta bringing in a group of specialised AI researchers and engineers rather than acquiring an entire startup.Meta continues AI safety pushDespite the departure of the Virtue AI team, Stone said Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.The development comes as AI companies face increasing scrutiny over how they develop, test and deploy increasingly capable systems. AI agents, in particular, have become a growing area of focus as companies work on systems that can perform more complex tasks with less human intervention.Meta's decision to recruit the Virtue AI team in June was part of that broader push. However, the arrangement lasted only four months before the company decided to let the employees go.Meta has made similar AI team hiresThe Virtue AI hiring was also part of Meta's broader strategy to recruit specialised teams from smaller AI companies.Meta poached the founders and team behind Dreamer, an AI startup focused on helping people build agents, in March. The approach allows the company to bring in specialised talent and expertise without necessarily acquiring an entire company.The Virtue AI departures now mark a much shorter-lived version of that strategy, with Meta confirming that differences in working styles contributed to the arrangement ending.The company, however, continues to expand its AI operations as the race to develop increasingly capable models and agents intensifies.You use AI every day. articles.title: She bought 3 Abbott shares for $180 in 1935; after her death at 100, her $7 million fortune went to help college students
articles.summary: Grace Groner lived a modest life in Lake Forest, Illinois, despite eventually accumulating a fortune worth more than $7 million.
articles.body: Grace Groner lived a modest life in Lake Forest, Illinois, despite eventually accumulating a fortune worth more than $7 million. She never married or had children, worked for more than four decades as a secretary at Abbott Laboratories and remained closely connected to Lake Forest College, where she graduated in 1931. When she died in January 2010 at the age of 100, she left her entire estate to a foundation benefiting students at her alma mater. Her fortune had grown from three Abbott shares she purchased for $60 each in 1935, an investment of $180 that she held for the rest of her life. Groner and her twin sister, Gladys, had been orphaned as children before the Anderson family took them in and helped support their education.How three Abbott shares became a multimillion-dollar fortuneGroner's extraordinary financial story began after she started working at Abbott Laboratories. According to the Grace Elizabeth Groner Foundation, she bought three shares of Abbott stock for $60 each in 1935. She held onto the investment and reinvested the dividends as the company continued to grow and its shares split over the following decades. The original $180 investment eventually became a fortune worth more than $7 million.Groner spent more than four decades working at Abbott as a secretary, but her lifestyle remained modest even as the value of her investment increased. She lived in a small one-bedroom cottage in Lake Forest rather than moving into a larger or more expensive home. Her attorney and longtime friend, William Marlatt, told contemporary reporters that Groner could have lived in any house in Lake Forest but chose not to. The precise value of her estate has been reported somewhat differently over the years. Contemporary coverage generally described it as about $7 million, while later accounts have cited figures around $7.2 million. Lake Forest College itself describes the gift as more than $7 million, making that the safest figure to use when describing the bequest.Grace Groner's connection to Lake Forest CollegeGroner's relationship with Lake Forest College began long before her fortune was known. She and her twin sister, Gladys, were orphaned when they were children and were taken in by the Anderson family of Lake Forest. The family helped the sisters attend boarding school and later supported their education at Lake Forest College, where Grace graduated in 1931.She remained involved with the college for decades after graduating. Before her death, Groner gave $180,000 to establish a scholarship programme intended to help students pursue internships and study-abroad opportunities. She also continued attending college events and maintaining a connection with the institution. Groner's charitable giving extended beyond the college. Contemporary reporting described her as someone who regularly made smaller donations to local causes, sometimes anonymously. Her lifelong pattern of giving meant that Lake Forest College knew her as a generous supporter, even though the institution did not know the full scale of her wealth.How a modest donor left a multimillion-dollar estateGroner had arranged for her estate to benefit Lake Forest College through a foundation. College president Stephen Schutt knew for more than a year before her death that she intended to leave her estate to the institution, but he did not know the eventual size of the gift. When Groner died in January 2010, the value of the estate revealed the extraordinary scale of the bequest.The Grace Elizabeth Groner Foundation was established to support qualified Lake Forest College students. Its current description says the foundation provides financial support to service-oriented students and helps fund service-learning opportunities in their communities, nationally and internationally. This includes opportunities that allow students to undertake service projects as part of their educational experience. Groner's former home also became part of her legacy. She left the cottage to Lake Forest College, and it became known as Grace's Cottage. The foundation says two female Lake Forest College seniors are invited to live there each year as Grace's guests. The cottage therefore became another way for her modest home to remain connected to the college and its students after her death.Why Grace Groner's story became a fundraising lessonThe size of Groner's bequest attracted attention in the fundraising world because her wealth was not apparent from her lifestyle. The Chronicle of Philanthropy reported on the case as a lesson for colleges seeking to identify potential estate donors. Fundraising writer Roger Craver pointed to characteristics in Groner's history that, in his view, could have indicated her potential, including her continued support for the college and her pattern of making smaller charitable gifts. Craver's interpretation should not be treated as a formula for predicting who will leave a large estate gift. What is documented is that Groner had maintained a long relationship with Lake Forest College, had given to the institution during her lifetime and had arranged for her estate to benefit it after her death. Her outwardly modest lifestyle did not reveal the value of the investment she had held for decades.Her story also emerged during a period when American universities were receiving a number of unexpectedly large anonymous donations. ABC News reported in 2010 that at least nine US universities had received gifts of more than $1 million from anonymous donors during the spring of 2009. The examples included an $8 million gift to Purdue University and a $6 million gift to the University of Southern Mississippi. Groner's bequest stood out because of the unusual path her money had taken. Three Abbott shares purchased for $180 in 1935 had grown through decades of holding and reinvested dividends into an estate worth more than $7 million. After her death, that wealth was redirected toward students at the college that had helped shape her early life, turning a quiet lifetime investment into a lasting source of educational support.You use AI every day. articles.title: LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman wants Americans to stop 'hating' datacentres; calls them the only reason US is not in a recession
articles.summary: LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman has defended the massive wave of AI infrastructure investment in the United States, arguing that spending on data centers
articles.body: LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman has defended the massive wave of AI infrastructure investment in the United States, arguing that spending on data centers and related projects is providing a significant boost to the broader economy and helping the country to avoid recession. According to a report by Benzinga, speaking on the Newcomer podcast, Hoffman said that billions of dollars flowing into AI infrastructure are generating economic activity far beyond technology companies. According to him, the current AI buildout is ‘the only reason we’re not in recession’, highlighting the role of a large-scale capital investments in supporting jobs and growth. He pushed back on the common perception that this investment narrowly benefits only tech companies, arguing that most of that capital doesn't actually concentrate in the specific areas where data centers are physically built, but instead ends up more broadly distributed across the country — a dynamic he described as a clear positive.Reid Hoffman defends AI infrastructure boomReid Hoffman emphasized the ripple effects this spending has on local economies, pointing to the range of workers who benefit from data center construction beyond the tech industry itself: construction workers, carpenters, real estate agents, electricians, and lawyers, among others. He argued that people tend to assume this capital infusion flows exclusively to tech companies, when in reality a massive percentage of it is actually going toward the physical work of building data centers themselves.Hoffman also said data center developers have a responsibility to work fairly with the local communities hosting these projects, framing it as essential that both developers and communities come away benefiting from the arrangement, rather than one side absorbing most of the costs or disruption.Context: a boom not without controversyHoffman's defense of data center spending comes amid a broader wave of scrutiny over how AI infrastructure investment is being financed and accounted for. Earlier this month, Meta reportedly classified some of its AI data centers as "pilot models" in order to claim federal research tax credits, a move that reduced the company's 2025 tax bill by $3.9 billion — though its own accountants reportedly warned that the IRS could challenge that classification.Separately, Broadcom was reportedly assembling a $60 billion financing package to help Anthropic and other companies fund their AI chip and infrastructure needs, a deal that could further expand AI capacity nationwide while simultaneously boosting demand for Broadcom's own data-center hardware.Not everyone shares Reid Hoffman's optimismHoffman's upbeat framing stands in contrast to warnings from other prominent voices in and around the industry. AI skeptic Ed Zitron warned last month that the private credit financing fueling the AI data-center boom had become what he called a "brewing crisis," citing rising borrowing costs and mounting construction delays as signs of real financial strain building beneath the surface.Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has also struck a more cautious tone, suggesting the world may need to experience a serious AI-related crisis, such as a major cyberattack or similar catastrophe, before governments and the public take the technology's risks seriously enough to respond with real urgency.You use AI every day. articles.title: How flydubai security failure, across 3 countries, almost led to 'Israel’s 9/11’
articles.summary: A string of security failures across Oman, the UAE and Israel allowed the flydubai co-pilot to get into the cockpit, a Wall Street Journal investigation
articles.body: A string of security failures across Oman, the UAE and Israel allowed the flydubai co-pilot to get into the cockpit, a Wall Street Journal investigation has found. The lapses nearly led to an aviation disaster reminiscent of 9/11, despite authorities having reasons to be concerned about him.The failures began in Oman, where authorities had scrutinised Hamam al-Hammami’s online activity and found he showed too much interest in radical ideology to be trusted as a pilot at state carrier Oman Air. They banned him from flying, sent him to a deradicalisation programme and moved him to a desk job, but did not broadly communicate their concerns about him.Oman flagged him, but the warning did not travelWhen al-Hammami joined flydubai in February, the airline did not contact Oman to vet his previous experience, the WSJ reported. It conducted a criminal-background check, but the earlier concerns that had led Oman to remove him from flying were not passed on to the new employer. The operator, flydubai, later assigned him to the sensitive Tel Aviv route, which he flew multiple times.Oman’s handling of the case also created another missed opportunity. People familiar with the matter said that had the country formally withdrawn al-Hammami’s pilot licence over its concerns, the action would likely have been flagged to the UAE. Instead, the concerns about his extremism were not communicated more widely.Israel had his name, and still let him flyThe final layer of failures came in Israel, where foreign airlines are required to submit passenger and crew lists before arriving.Airline operator flydubai had submitted the manifest for Flight 1073, but Israel’s transportation ministry said it did not believe it had the authority or expertise to vet foreign flight crews. The ministry also said it had never asked to access a database created in 2023 to help authorised agencies review passenger and crew information because it did not know the database was operational or that it could use it.There was an even more basic warning that should have stopped al-Hammami from flying to Israel. Pilots from countries such as Oman, which does not have diplomatic relations with Israel, are barred from flying to the country. Yet al-Hammami was allowed onto the Tel Aviv-bound flight.Israel’s own previous warnings also raise questions about how the system failed. A classified May 2024 report by the country’s comptroller general had warned that aviation security had grown lax, with fragmented responsibilities and unclear lines of authority. The report also identified manpower and budget problems affecting oversight by the transportation ministry.The cockpit attackThe security failures culminated halfway through Flight 1073, when al-Hammami attacked Captain Smit Machchhar with an emergency axe after excusing himself to pray.The wounded captain managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and others to enter and overpower the co-pilot. They then helped pull the aircraft out of a dangerous dive.The UAE’s attorney general has described the incident as an attempted terrorist act. Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Israel suspect al-Hammami was trying to crash the aircraft in Tel Aviv, according to people familiar with their thinking. All three countries are investigating whether he acted alone; so far, investigators have not found links to a foreign power or major terrorist organisation, those people said.The incident has since prompted Israel to review the security of foreign airline flights to the country.You use AI every day. articles.title: Guam's snake invasion became so bad that power lines were a problem: How brown tree snakes climbed poles, caused blackouts and forced researchers to find bizarre ways to keep them away
articles.summary: Guam’s brown tree snake problem is far stranger than a typical invasive-species story.
articles.body: Guam’s brown tree snake problem is far stranger than a typical invasive-species story. The snakes did not simply spread through forests and prey on native wildlife. They learned to exploit the island’s infrastructure too, climbing poles, reaching electrical equipment and triggering costly power failures.The brown treesnake (Boiga irregularis) arrived on Guam sometime after World War II, probably as a stowaway in cargo. With few natural controls and plenty of prey, its population exploded. The consequences were severe for native birds and eventually reached something far less wild: the electrical grid.When a snake became an electrical problemBrown tree snakes are excellent climbers. They can move onto guy wires, poles, transformers and other electrical structures. When a snake touches two electrical points at once, its body can effectively bridge the circuit.The result can be a short circuit, electrical fault or surge. The snake may be electrocuted, while transformers and other equipment can also be damaged.The problem is not new. More than 1,600 snake-caused outages were recorded between 1978 and 1997, and older estimates put the annual economic impact at more than $4.5 million over a seven-year period.The snake that found a way around barriersThe strangest part came when researchers tried to stop the snakes from climbing smooth cylinders.Scientists discovered that brown tree snakes could form their bodies into a loop resembling a lasso. They use that loop as an anchor, then make small waves with the rest of the body to inch upward.Researchers named this previously undocumented movement “lasso locomotion.” It allows the snakes to climb smooth, wide cylinders that would defeat more conventional climbing movements. The discovery also explained why some seemingly clever barriers were not as snake-proof as expected.Then came the parachuting miceGuam’s snake-control efforts have produced one of the strangest wildlife-control methods ever attempted.Researchers discovered that acetaminophen is toxic to brown tree snakes. Instead of scattering bait across the forest floor, wildlife managers developed a way to place treated dead mice high in the canopy, where the snakes naturally hunt.Helicopters were used to release dead mice containing acetaminophen. Small cardboard-and-paper devices slowed their descent and helped the baits become caught in vegetation rather than simply falling to the ground.The method was designed to target snakes while reducing exposure to other wildlife. It has been used as a targeted control tool, not as a solution capable of eliminating Guam’s entire snake population.Dogs, traps and better barriers joined the fightThere is no single fix for an invasion this deeply established. Researchers have therefore tried several approaches, including traps, improved barriers, toxic baits and detection methods.Specially trained detector dogs can help locate brown tree snakes, while rapid-response teams work to intercept snakes that may leave Guam aboard ships or aircraft. That matters because Guam is a major Pacific transportation hub, making accidental spread to places such as Hawaii and the Northern Mariana Islands a continuing concern.The brown tree snake story shows how an invasive animal can reshape an island far beyond its forests.It has been linked to the decline or local extinction of many native bird species. It has disrupted electrical infrastructure and created an expensive maintenance problem. And its ability to hitchhike in cargo means Guam's problem could become another island's problem if prevention fails.Perhaps the most striking lesson is that wildlife does not always stay on the side of the landscape humans consider “natural.” On Guam, the snake adapted to poles, wires and other structures with surprising ease. The response had to become equally inventive.Disclaimer: This article is based on information from the U.S. Geological Survey and published scientific research. Control methods described above are specialized wildlife-management techniques and should not be attempted by the public.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates.
